definition: Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) is an independent federal corporation created by the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) of 1974 to insure defined-benefit pension plans and protect retirement benefits for participants and beneficiaries when covered private-sector plans fail. The PBGC insures plans under two programs: single-employer plans sponsored by individual employers or affiliated groups, and multiemployer plans maintained under collective bargaining agreements, but it does not cover defined-contribution plans such as 401(k)s. The PBGC is led by a director who is appointed by the President and is confirmed by the Senate, and it operates under a Board of Directors. When a covered plan terminates with insufficient assets to pay benefits, the PBGC typically becomes the trustee and pays benefits up to statutory limits that are adjusted annually. The maximum guarantee limits for plans are set by law and actuarial tables (see: mortality tables and monthly maximum tables. The PBGC is funded primarily by insurance premiums paid by plan sponsors, assets of plans it takes over, recoveries from plan sponsors in bankruptcy, and investment income. The PBGC also administers programs such as Special Financial Assistance to support severely underfunded multiemployer plans and produces annual reports and guidance for participants and plan sponsors.
